Pharmacy  Science  Event  Category:  Health  Professions
………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/Collegiate   
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  **HOSA  provides  a  basic  hand-held  calculator  for  this  test.   
Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor  Round  Two:  Skill(s)  assessment   
New  for  2026-2027
 Editorial  changes  have  been  made.  Ofﬁcial  resources  have  changed.  The  following  resources  have  been  deleted:   The  Pharmacy  Technician:   Foundations  and  Practices  and  Sterile  Compounding  and  Aseptic  Technique:   Concepts,                  Training,  and  Assessment .  Note  additional  resources  have  been  added  to  the  ofﬁcial  resources  listed  below.  A  special                  landing  page  has  been  added.    
Event  Summary
 Pharmacy  Science  enables  members  to  acquire  the  knowledge  and  skills  necessary  for  careers  in  pharmacy.  This  competitive  
event
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
rounds.
 
Round
 
One
 
is
 
a
 
written,
 
multiple-choice
 
test,
 
and
 
the
 
top-scoring
 
competitors
 
advance
 
to
 
Round
 
Two
 
for
 
the
 
skills
 
assessment.
 
This
 
event
 
aims
 
to
 
inspire
 
members
 
to
 
learn
 
more
 
about
 
the
 
ﬁeld
 
of
 
pharmacy,
 
including
 
careers
 
and
 
practices.
 
  
Sponsorship
 
HOSA-  Future  Health  Professionals  appreciates  the  sponsorship  of  this  event  by  the  ASHP.  ASHP  has  developed  a  special  landing  page for  HOSA  competitors  and  advisors.     
 
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   ●  Round  One:  Proper  business  attire,  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform,  or  attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area.    ●  Round  Two:  Attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area.  
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID for  both  rounds  ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  erasers  for  the  test.  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (Rd1-optional)  ●  Ink  pen  ●  Shoe  covers  ●  Face  mask  ●  Hair  cover  ●  Beard  cover  (if  appropriate)  ●  Hair  Tie  to  pull  back  long  hair  (if  appropriate)  ●  Non-shedding  gown  with  snug-ﬁtting  cuffs   ●  Eye  shields  or  goggles  ●  Sterile,  powder-free,  latex-free  gloves  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
 Pharmacy  Science  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  21  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.

The  following  additional  resource  is  available  at  HOSA  Webinars:  ASHP  -  The  Pharmacy  Files.   
 
ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  answer  sheet.   The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here.  At  the  International  Leadership  Conference,  HOSA  will  provide  basic  handheld  calculators  (no  graphing  calculators)  for  addition,  subtraction,  division,  multiplication,  and  square  root.    USE  OF  ZERO:  Decimal  expressions  of  less  than  1  should  be  preceded  by  a  zero—a  “leading  zero.”   A  whole  number  should  never  be  followed  by  a  decimal  point  and  a  zero  –  “trailing  zero.”  
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.   All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
Written  Test  Plan  The  written  test  for  Pharmacy  Science  is:  ●  Pharmacy  Practice  History  &  Practice  Settings  -  4%  ●  Pharmacy  Law  &  Ethics  and  Safety  &  Infection  Control  -  10%  ●  Pharmacy  Terminology  &  Abbreviations  -  10%  ●  Dosage  Formulations  &  Administration  Routes  -  10%  ●  Sterile  and  Non-Sterile  Compounding  -  10%  ●  Concentration  &  Dilutions  -  10%  ●  Disorders  &  Treatments  -  46%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  What  is  the  term  for  the  study  of  the  movement  of  a  drug  through  body  systems,  including  absorption,  distribution,  metabolism,  and  excretion?  (Stuham   pp  19)                    A.     Pharmacology                    B.     Pharmacokinetics                    C.     Therapeutics                    D.     Pharmacogenomics   2.  What  law  was  passed  in  1938  which  began  to  regulate  drugs  and  prohibit  false  therapeutic       claims?  (  Bachenheimer  &  Phillips  pp  53)                    A.     Durham-Humphrey  Amendment                    B.     Omnibus  Budget  Reconciliation  Act                    C.     Harris  Narcotic  Tax  Act                     D.     Food,  Drug,  and  Cosmetic  Act  
 Pharmacy  Science  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  2  of  21  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

 3.  If  a  patient  is  to  receive  1  ounce  of  an  over-the-counter  medication,  how  many  tablespoons   should  be  given?  (Bachenheimer  &  Phillips  pp  325)                    A.    1  tablespoon                     B.    2  tablespoons                    C.    3  tablespoons                    D.    4.  tablespoons   
ROUND  TWO-  Skill  Assessment
 
1.  The  top  competitors  from  Round  One  will  advance  to  Round  Two.  The  number  of  advancing  competitors  will  be  determined  by  the  scores  obtained  in  Round  One  and  the  space  and  time  available  for  Round  Two.  Round  Two  ﬁnalists  will  be  announced  on-site  at  ILC  per  the  conference  agenda.  
2.  Round  Two  is  a  selected  skill(s)  assessment.  The  skills  approved  for  this  event  are:  
Skill  I:  Identifying  Instrument/Equipment  (including  name  of  instrument  and  purpose  of  use)  **See  list  of  instruments  below  
15  minutes   
Skill  II:  Verifying  the  Content  of  a  Controlled  Substance  Prescription  and  DEA  Number   6  minutes  
Skill  III:  Withdrawing  Liquid  from  a  Vial   15  minutes  
Skill  IV:  Compounding  an  Oral  Suspension  15  minutes  
Skill  V:  Patient  Screening  for  Pharmacist  Consultation  and  Services  4  minutes  
Skill  VI:  Filling  A  Prescription  5  minutes  
Skill  VII:  Aseptic  Garbing,  Hand  Washing  and  Gloving  10  minutes  3.  Skill  I  may  be  administered  with  the  Round  One  written  test.  If  this  skill  is  administered  with  written  test,  the  skill  assessment  allotted  time  will  be  added  to  the  written  test  allotted  time.    4.  For  all  skills,  body  ﬂuids  and  medications  will  be  simulated  products.   
Below  is  the  list  of  equipment/instruments  used  for  the  Skill  I:  Identify  Instruments/Equipment.  Could  be  15  numbered  photos  or  images.  Ampules  Forceps  -  Tissue  Liquid  Oral  Syringe  Spatula  Autoclave  Forceps  -  Hemostatic  Medicine  Cup  Stirring  Rods  Auxiliary  Labels  Graduated  Cylinders  Liquid  Oral  Syringe  Suppository  Mold  –  Aluminum  Type  Beaker  Tongs  Eyewash  Station  Medicine  Cup  Suppository  Mold  –  Plastic  Type  Beakers  Heat  Gun  Medicine  Dropper  Syringes  Calibrated  Spoon  Hot  Plate  Mortar  Tablet  Mold  Compounding  Slabs  or  Disposable  Slabs  
Indicator  Strip  (used  for  sterilization)  
Pestle  Transdermal  Patch  
Conical  Graduates  Insulin  Syringes  Pipettes  Tuberculin  Syringe  Counting  Trays  Intravenous  Injection  Safety  Syringes  Ultrasonic  Cleaning  Unit  Crimper  Laminar  Airﬂow  Hood  Sharps  Container  Weights  
 
5.   The  selected  skill(s)  will  be  presented  to  competitors  as  a  written  scenario  at  the  beginning  of  the                 round.  The  scenario  will  be  the  same  for  each  competitor.  Some  scenarios  may  involve  the  combination                 of  multiple  skills.  In  the  event  rating  sheets  are  combined,  it  is  not  necessary  to  repeat  a  task  a  second   
 Pharmacy  Science  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  3  of  21  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

              time.  An  example  would  be  that  competitors  would  not  need  to  identify  the  patient  twice.  A  sample                 scenario  is  available  here.  
6.  Timing  will  begin  when  the  scenario  is  presented  to  the  competitors  and  will  be  stopped  at  the  end  of  the  time    allowed.  The  scenario  is  a  secret  topic.  Competitors  MAY  NOT  discuss  or  reveal  the  secret  topic  until  after  the  event  has  concluded  or  will  face  penalties  per  the  GRRs.   
7.  Competitors  must  complete  all  skill  steps  listed  in  the  guidelines,  even  if  the  steps  must  be  simulated/  verbalized.  (If  the  equipment  is  available,  the  competitors  would  complete  all  skill  steps  as  the  scenario  warrants.  The  competitors  will  simulate/verbalize  the  steps  if  the  equipment  is  unavailable.)  
8.  Judges  will  provide  information  to  competitors  as  directed  by  the  rating  sheets.  Competitors  may  ask  questions  of  the  judges  while  performing  skills,  if  the  questions  relate  to  patient’s  condition  and  will  be  included  in  the  scenario  or  judge  script.  
9.  Competitors  must  use  all  equipment  correctly  and  safely.  Judges  will  stop  a  student  and  not  award  points  for  a  step  if  they  see  a  competitor  is  about  to  cause  a  risk  of  harm  or  about  to  damage  equipment  or  other  supplies.   
Final  Scoring 
 1.  The  competitor  must  earn  a  score  of  70%  or  higher  on  the  combined  skill(s)  in  Round  Two-Skills  Assessment   
(excluding

test
 
and
 
Identifying
 
Equipment)
 
in
 
order
 
to
 
be
 
recognized
 
as

award
 
winner
 
at
 
the
 
ILC.
 
  2.  The  ﬁnal  rank  is  determined  by  adding  the  round  one  test  score  plus  the  round  two  skill  score.  In  the  event  of  a  tie,  
the
 
highest
 
test
 
score
 
will
 
be
 
used
 
to
 
determine
 
the
 
ﬁnal
 
placement.

Pharmacy  Science  Skill  II:  Verifying  the  Content  of  a  Controlled  Substance  Prescription  and  DEA  Number  
 
***  Via  the  event  scenario,  the  competitor  will  be  given  a  prescription.  Each  competitor  will  also  be  given  a  Prescription  Veriﬁcation  Form,  which  acts  as  the  rating  sheet  (page  7  of  the  guidelines).  The  prescription  in  the  scenario  will  have  missing  information.  Competitors  must  know  all  the  prescription  components  (below)  to  identify  which  components  are  missing.  The  judges  will  score  the  Prescription  Veriﬁcation  Form  using  the  points  indicated.   
When  verifying  a  Controlled  Substance  Prescription  with  DEA  Number,  the  below  list  of  items  must  all  be  veriﬁed.   
1.  Patient  Information  a.  Name  b.  Address  c.  Date  of  Birth  2.  Prescriber  Information  a.  Name  b.  Address  c.  Telephone  Number  d.  License  Number  3.  DEA  Number  a.  Veriﬁed  the  second  letter  corresponds  to  the  ﬁrst  letter  of  the  provider’s  last  name  b.  Added  the  ﬁrst,  third,  and  ﬁfth  digits  of  the  DEA  number.  c.  Added  the  second,  fourth,  and  sixth  digits  of  the  DEA  number.  Double  the  sum.  d.  Added  the  sum  of  b  and  c.   e.  Veriﬁed  that  the  last  digit  from  step  d  matches  the  last  digit  of  the  DEA  number.  4.  When  prescribed  a.  Month  b.  Day  c.  Year  5.  Drug  name  and  strength  6.  Dose  and  quantity  7.  Route  of  administration  8.  Directions  (signature  or  “Sig”)  9.  Number  of  reﬁlls  authorized  10.  Product  selection  was  permitted  11.  Prescriber’s  signature  12.  No  dangerous  abbreviations,  acronyms,  or  symbols  are  used  from  the  Joint  Commission’s  “Minimum”  Do  Not  Use  list  and  the  Joint  Commission’s  “Recommended”  Do  Not  Use  List.

 Skill  III:  Withdrawing  Liquid  from  a  Vial  
Possible  Awarded  
    1.    Obtained  the  medication  order.  
1  0    
    2.    Obtained  needed  supplies  and  placed  in  a  transport  vehicle.     
1  0    
3.    Performed  calculation  based  on  scenario.  
      4        0    
4.    Verbalized:  “I  have  donned  PPE  and  washed  my  hands,and  donned  sterile  gloves.”  
2  0    
           
    
CLEAN
 
ROOM
 
PROCEDURE
 
5.   
 Verbalized  cleaning  the  hood  - competitor  included  which  surface  cleaned  with  what    supplies. 
2  0    
6.    Placed  all  supply  items  for  the  skill  into  the  outer  six-inch  staging  area  of   the  hood.    
1  0    
7.    Placed  the  vial  within  the  Direct  Compounding  Area  (DCA).   
1  0    
8.    Removed  the  ﬂip-top  cap  and  placed  it  in  the  discard  pile.  
1  0    
9.   
 Opened  an  alcohol  swab  within  the  Direct  Compounding  Area  and  placed  the  wrapper  on  the   discard  pile.  
1  0    
10.   
 Placed  the  used  swab  on  the  hood’s  work  surface  within  the  DCA.  Swabbed  the  top  of  the   medicine  vial  and  discarded  the  used  swab  in  the  discard  pile.   
2  0    
11.    Swabbed  the  top  of  the  medicine  vial  and  discarded  the  used  swab  in  the   discard  pile.   
1  0    
12.  
 Aseptically  attached  a  needle  to  the  syringe  and  gently  screwed   the  needle  hub  onto  the    syringe  tip.    
2  0    
13.  
 Pulled  the  plunger  back  on  the  syringe  to  slightly  less  than  the  amount  needed  to  be  drawn   up.  
1  0    
14.    Removed  the  needle  cap  and  placed  it  onto  the  alcohol  swab.  
2  0    
15.   
 Used  the  thumb  and  foreﬁnger  of  the  nondominant  hand,  to  stabilize  the  vial  against  the   hood’s  work  surface.  
1  0    
16.   Placed  the  needle  tip  bevel  up  and  inserted  at  a  45-degree  angle  through  the  stopper.   
1  0    
17.   Gently  pushed  the  air  from  the  syringe  into  the  vial.  
1  0    
18.  
 Used  nondominant  hand  holding  the  vial  and  the  dominant  hand  to  maintain  the  needle  in    the  vial  while  inverting  the  vial  so  that  needle  and   syringe  is  below  the  vial.  
1  0    
19.  
 Allowed  ﬂuid  to  move  from  the  vial  to  syringe.   If  needed,  pulled  back  on  the  plunger  until   the  desired  amount  is  withdrawn.  
1  0    
20.  
 Checked  syringe  contents  for  bubbles  and  taped  syringe  to  move  air   bubbles  to  hub,  then    push  bubbles  into  the  vial.  
2  0    
21.   Withdrew  needle  from  vial.    
1  0    
22.   Carefully  recapped  needle.

Pharmacy Science 
Skill IV: Compounding an Oral Suspension 
Time: 15 minutes 
Competitor  #:___________________________     Division: _______SS ________PS/C    Judge’s Signature:____________________________ 
Skill IV: Compounding an Oral Suspension Possible Awarded 
1.  Obtained the completed recipe or completed formula via scenario using the Master Formula 
 sheet.  1  0 
2.  Checked the amount per dose and the total volume needed to be prepared with the 
 pharmacist (judge).   2  0 
3.  Used Master Formula sheet to obtain needed medication: 
a. Obtained the correct number of tablets needed.  2  0 
b. veriﬁed with pharmacist (judge) both the drug product selected and the number of
tablets needed for compounding, based on the Master Formula Sheet  2  0 
* Judge veriﬁed accuracy. The competitor proceeds either way. Points only awarded if the correct number of tablets were
obtained.
4.  Obtained needed equipment 1 0 
5.  Washed hands or used alcohol based hand-rub for hand hygiene. 2 0 
6.  Donned or verbalized donning personal protective equipment:  hair cover, face mask, gloves, 
 and gown. 
2 0 
7.  Crushed or reduced to a ﬁne powder by using mortar and pestle. 1 0 
8.  Added a small amount of suspending vehicle to wet the powder, and then mixed (levigated) 
 the powder with the liquid until a smooth paste is formed.   1 0 
9. Continued to add suspending vehicle until product is liquid enough to transfer to a 
graduated cylinder.  1 0 
10.  Poured the liquid into a graduated cylinder. 1 0 
11.  Rinsed mortar several times with small amounts of suspending vehicle and added to the 
 product in the graduated cylinder. 1 0 
12.  Added suspending vehicle to bring product up to the required ﬁnal volume and veriﬁed the 
 amount of suspension at eye level. 2 0 
13.  Poured the compounded suspension into the most appropriately sized amber oval medication 
 bottle, sealed bottle and shook well.   1 0 
14. Selected the appropriate label from those provided and afﬁxed to the medication bottle. 
*Judge veriﬁed accuracy.  Points awarded only if the correct label(s) was selected and afﬁxed.
4 0 
*Judge veriﬁed accuracy. Points awarded only if the correct label(s) was selected and afﬁxed.
15.  Selected the appropriate auxiliary label(s) from those provided and afﬁxed to the medication 
 bottle. 4 0 
*Judge veriﬁed accuracy. Points only awarded if the correct label was selected and afﬁxed.
16.  Cleaned the compounding area and equipment using 70% isopropyl alcohol and wipes and 
 returned equipment to proper place. 2 0 
17.  Removed and disposed of PPE. 2 0 
18.  Washed hands or used alcohol based hand-rub for hand hygiene. 2 0

Screening  Checklist  for  Contraindications  to  Injectable  Inactivated  
Poliovirus
 
Vaccination
 
 For  patients  (both  children  and  adults)  to  be  vaccinated:   The  questions  asked  are  developed  to  determine  if  the  requested  
vaccination
 
should
 
be
 
given.
  
If
 
you
 
answer
 
“yes”
 
to
 
any
 
of
 
the
 
following
 
questions,
 
it
 
does
 
not
 
necessarily
 
mean
 
the
 
vaccination
 
will
 
not
 
be
 
given.
  
Additional
 
information
 
will
 
be
 
required.
            1.   Does  the  person  to  be  vaccinated  have  allergies  to  any  component  of  the  vaccine?        2.   Is  the  person  to  be  vaccinated  today  immune  depressed  in  any  way?     3.  Does  the  person  to  be  vaccinated  live  with  anyone  who  has  an  immune  deﬁciency  disease?     4.   Is  there  a  suspected  familial  immune  deﬁciency?     5.   Is  there  a  possibility  that  the  person  being  vaccinated  is  pregnant?            Reference:  Moini,  Jahangir.   The  Pharmacy  Technician:   A  Comprehensive  Approach.   Cengage  Learning,  latest  edition.    Screening  Checklist  will  not  be  provided  during  the  event.   Competitors  will  need  to  memorize  the  questions  related  to  the  identiﬁed  
issue.

Skill  V:  Patient  Screening  for  Pharmacist  Consultation  and  Services  
                             
Screening  Checklist  for  Late  Reﬁll      Promoting  compliance  with  prescribed  medication  is  an  important  role  of  the  pharmacy  staff.   If  the  patient  is  not  taking  
medication
 
as
 
prescribed
 
the
 
following
 
questions
 
may
 
help
 
determine
 
the
 
cause
 
of
 
noncompliance.
                     1.   How  did  the  prescriber  recommend  you  take  this  medication?   2.   What  methods  do  you  use  to  help  remember  to  take  your  medication?    3.   What  side  effects  have  you  experienced  with  the  medication?   4.   Has  this  medication  helped  relieve  conditions  for  which  it  was  prescribed?      5.   Are  there  any  other  reasons  you  do  not  take  this  medication  as  often  as  prescribed?

PHARMACY  SCIENCE
  
Skill  V:  Patient  Screening  for  Pharmacist  Consultation  and  Services  
Screening  Checklist  for  Possible  Allergic  Reaction  
 
 Allergic  reactions  can  be  life-threatening.  The  patient's  concerns  must  be  investigated.  The  following  questions  should  be  
asked
 
to
 
obtain
 
the
 
basic
 
information
 
needed.
                     1.   What  medication  were  you  taking  when  you  noticed  symptoms  of  concern?    2.  Please  describe  your  symptoms.    3.   When  did  your  symptoms  begin?   4.   Were  any  other  medications  taken  during  this  time,  including  over-the-counter  drugs?        5.   Have  you  stopped  taking  the  medication?

 Skill  VI:  Filling  a  Prescription  
Possible  Awarded  
1.    Obtained  prescription.   
1  0    
2.   
 Reviewed  the  prescription  for  legality  and  correctness.  a.  Veriﬁed  the  patient  name  on  the  prescription  by  asking  the  patient.  
2  0    
 
b.  The  date  for  the  presented  prescription  was  written  within  the  past  year.  
2  0    c.  Veriﬁed  address  of  the  patient.  
1  0    d.  Date  of  birth  veriﬁed  
1  0    
3.

2  0

2  0

2  0

4  0    
9.   
 Used  the  counting  tray  and  spatula  to  count  needed  number  of  tablets  or  capsules  for  the   current  prescription.    
4  0

2  0    
11.   
 Obtained  the  most  appropriate  container  (type  and  shape)  for  the  prescription  from  those   supplied.   
1  0    
12.   Obtained  the  correct  label, rechecking  the  directions  and   drug  strength.   
4  0    
13.   Afﬁxed  auxiliary  labels  if  indicated  such  as  take  with  meals,  shake  well,  etc.    
2  0    
14.    Submitted  to  pharmacist  (judge)  for  ﬁnal  check.    
4  0    
              *Judge  veriﬁed  accuracy  of  ﬁnal  product  
15.    Avoided  contamination  by  not  touching  medication  directly  throughout  ﬁlling  process.    
2  0    
16.  
 Cleaned  counting  tray  and  spatula  with  an  alcohol  swab.  
2  0    
17.  
 Returned  all  equipment  to  appropriate  place.
